patients.summary: Retired shipyard boiler technician with insulin-treated diabetes, PAD, venous ulcer disease, COPD and decompensated hepatitis C and alcohol cirrhosis who joins in 2020 with a new rectal cancer. Over six years he develops asbestosis, radiation proctitis, a Marjolin's ulcer, hepatocellular carcinoma, pancreatic carcinoma with bone metastasis, emphysematous cholecystitis and fulminant C. difficile colitis; last seen in the practice April 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64M here to establish. His longtime PCP is retiring at the end of the month and he wanted somebody he could reach by phone given everything going on.

HPI: A lot at once. Rectal bleeding in the spring led to a colonoscopy in July; rectal adenocarcinoma, staged IIIB. Oncology has him starting pelvic chemoradiation in September with surgery after. He is anxious about it but practical. Otherwise his chronic issues:
- DM2 on glargine 24 qHS and lispro 8 with meals plus a correction scale. Checks fingersticks 3-4x a day, mornings 130s-170s, no lows he can recall.
- Cirrhosis: hep C (genotype 1a) plus decades of drinking, diagnosed 2017 when he presented with fluid in the belly and confusion. Treated for hep C in 2018 by his hepatologist and was told it was cured. Has not had a drink since 2017. On furosemide 40 bid, spironolactone 100, lactulose (2-3 BMs a day, sometimes 4) and rifaximin. Hepatology sees him every 6 months with ultrasound.
- PAD: right fem-pop bypass in March of this year. Walks a few blocks.
- Venous disease left leg with a long-standing ulcer above the ankle; graft in May, partly taken. Wound clinic every few weeks. Pentoxifylline. Oxycodone 5 mg, usually 1-2 a day, for leg pain and achy knees/hands.
- COPD on tiotropium daily, albuterol a few times a week.
- Prostate cancer 2017: radical prostatectomy then radiation to the prostate bed. Urology checks PSA yearly, always undetectable or near it.
- CKD 3a per old labs. On aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, metoprolol for his vascular disease.

PMH/PSH: as above. Prostatectomy 2017. R fem-pop 03/2020. L leg skin graft 05/2020.
Meds: reviewed bottle by bottle, 14 items, list reconciled.
Allergies: sulfa (rash). IV contrast dye (anaphylaxis, years ago with a CT).
FH: father died of pancreatic cancer at 72. Mother died at 78 of emphysema. Paternal uncle died of colon cancer at 68. One brother, treated for prostate cancer.
SH: Retired 2017 from the shipyard where he worked as a boiler tech. Smoked about 40 pack-years, quit 2017. Heavy drinker for about 30 years, none since 2017. No drugs.

ROS: fatigue, otherwise negative except as above.

Exam: Thin older man, no distress. Mild scleral icterus. Lungs: diminished breath sounds, no wheeze or crackles. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abd: soft, mildly protuberant, flanks dull, non-tender. Ext: healed R thigh/knee incisions; L lower leg with hemosiderin staining, graft site medial ankle with a small open area about 1.5 cm, clean base, dressing in place; trace edema. Pedal pulses diminished bilaterally. Feet: no other skin breakdown, monofilament intact. Neuro: alert, oriented, no asterixis.

A/P:
1. Rectal adenocarcinoma IIIB - oncology/radiation leading. We will be the home base; asked him to send any letters our way.
2. DM2 - A1c today. Same insulin.
3. Cirrhosis, decompensated - CMP, CBC, INR today; confirm HCV RNA negative since we have no paperwork. Continue diuretics, lactulose, rifaximin.
4. CKD 3a - BMP part of CMP, UACR.
5. PAD/venous ulcer - per vascular and wound clinic.
6. COPD - stable.
7. Health maintenance - HIV screen today (never done). Flu and pneumococcal next visit. Records requested from prior office and specialists.
Follow up 6 weeks.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Peter, your labs are back. Hep C virus test is negative, so the 2018 treatment worked. HIV screen negative. A1c 7.6, a little above where I'd like it but fine for now with everything you have going on. Kidney function is in your usual range. Liver numbers (bilirubin, albumin, clotting) fit your known cirrhosis, nothing new. Blood count is slightly low, which we'll keep an eye on through treatment. No changes. See you in October.

documents.title: Medical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 08/31/2020
Re: Peter Kimball, DOB 01/30/1956
Copy to: primary care physician

Reason: newly diagnosed rectal adenocarcinoma.

Mr. Kimball is a 64-year-old man with decompensated cirrhosis (HCV, treated, and prior alcohol), insulin-treated diabetes, PAD and a 2017 prostatectomy with adjuvant prostate-bed radiation, who had hematochezia this spring. Colonoscopy 07/09/2020 found a mid-rectal mass; biopsies show moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Pelvic MRI and staging imaging show regional nodal disease and no distant metastases: clinical stage IIIB.

Allergies: sulfonamides (rash); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis) - staging done without iodinated contrast.

Assessment and plan: Locally advanced rectal cancer. We discussed long-course chemoradiation followed by resection. Radiation oncology has reviewed his prior prostate-bed fields and will plan around them. Concurrent capecitabine 1500 mg twice daily on radiation days, dose chosen with his liver function in mind; weekly CBC and CMP during treatment. Systemic chemotherapy beyond the radiosensitizing dose is not advisable with Child-Pugh C cirrhosis. Start 09/08/2020. Colorectal surgery referral for after completion.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.
Medical Oncology

documents.title: Colorectal Surgery Consultation
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
COLORECTAL SURGERY CONSULTATION, 01/12/2021
Patient: Peter Kimball
Referred by: Medical Oncology; cc PCP

Stage IIIB mid-rectal adenocarcinoma, completed long-course chemoradiation with capecitabine 10/16/2020. Restaging MRI shows partial response with no new disease. Comorbidities are substantial: Child-Pugh C cirrhosis with ascites controlled on diuretics, insulin-treated diabetes, PAD with recent right fem-pop, COPD.
Allergies: sulfonamides, iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Exam: thin, no distress. Abdomen soft, mildly distended, no hernia. DRE deferred today.

Plan: Low anterior resection with diverting loop ileostomy, tentatively 02/23/2021. Operative risk with his liver disease was discussed openly and he wishes to proceed. Needs pre-operative evaluation from PCP, hepatology input on peri-operative ascites management, and anesthesia review. Stoma teaching scheduled.
Colorectal Surgery

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op eval for LAR with diverting loop ileostomy planned 2/23 by colorectal surgery.

S: Turned 65 last month. Feels as well as he has in a while. Walks ~2 blocks before calf aching, unchanged since bypass. No chest pain, no exertional pressure, no syncope. Breathing at baseline, no recent exacerbation. Sugars ok. No confusion, 3 BMs/day.
O: Vitals as charted. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. Heart RRR no murmur. Abd soft, mild shifting dullness, NT. L ankle ulcer small and clean. ECG: NSR, normal.
A/P: Elevated but accepted risk, driven by liver disease (Child-Pugh C) more than heart or lungs. No active cardiac conditions; functional capacity limited by claudication rather than angina; no further cardiac testing would change management.
- Continue aspirin per surgeon's preference (they asked to keep it), metoprolol and statin through surgery.
- Hold amlodipine morning of surgery if SBP low.
- Insulin: glargine 80% (19 units) the night before; hold lispro while NPO, correction scale in hospital.
- Diuretics: hold morning of surgery; hepatology aware.
- Continue lactulose/rifaximin post-op as soon as he can take PO; watch for encephalopathy with opioids.
- No iodinated contrast - anaphylaxis.
Letter faxed to surgeon.

events.reason: Low anterior resection with diverting loop ileostomy

reports.text: Specimen: rectosigmoid and rectum, low anterior resection. Residual moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with treatment effect, invading into the muscularis propria. Proximal, distal and radial margins negative. Lymph nodes negative for carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: Residual rectal adenocarcinoma after neoadjuvant therapy; all margins negative.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Colorectal Surgery
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Admission 02/23/2021 - Discharge 03/01/2021
Procedure 02/23/2021: low anterior resection with diverting loop ileostomy.
Indication: stage IIIB rectal adenocarcinoma after neoadjuvant chemoradiation.
Course: Uncomplicated operation. Post-op ileus resolved day 3. Ascites managed with resumption of home diuretics on day 2; no paracentesis needed. Lactulose resumed on day 2 at a reduced dose and opioids kept to a minimum; no confusion. Glucose managed with basal insulin plus correction. Ileostomy functioning, output 800-1200 mL/day at discharge. Stoma nurse teaching completed.
Pathology: residual adenocarcinoma, margins negative (see report).
Discharge medications: home list resumed unchanged; lactulose dose per ostomy output (aim for no confusion, not a set number of BMs).
Allergies: sulfonamides, iodinated contrast.
Follow-up: colorectal clinic 2 weeks; oncology 4 weeks; PCP 2-3 weeks. Reversal planned in about 6 months. No adjuvant chemotherapy recommended given liver function.

documents.title: Office Visit - post-op
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Four weeks after LAR with loop ileostomy. Incision healed. Ostomy output 1-1.5 L/day, mostly thick; empties bag 5-6x a day. Drinking well. Lactulose down to 15 mL bid per surgery with ostomy, no confusion. Glucose a bit lower since surgery, a few 90s fasting, no lows below 70. O: Vitals as charted. Midline incision healed. RLQ stoma pink, appliance intact, output thick brown. Abd soft, NT, no tense ascites. L ankle ulcer unchanged.
A/P:
- Ileostomy: output acceptable; push oral fluids; BMP today for sodium/potassium/creatinine since he's on two diuretics with a high-output stoma.
- If BMP shows creatinine up we'll trim furosemide. Hepatology aware.
- DM2: same insulin, call for any reading <80.
RTC 6-8 weeks or sooner.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Peter, kidney function and potassium are in your usual range, so no change. Keep the diuretics as they are and keep up the fluids with the ostomy. Let me know if you have dark urine or very high bag output.

documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
HEPATOLOGY, 05/20/2021
Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Kimball for his six-month review of cirrhosis (HCV genotype 1a with SVR after 2018 treatment, and prior alcohol, abstinent since 2017), Child-Pugh C. He came through his low anterior resection in February without encephalopathy. Diuretic-controlled ascites; no GI bleeding.
Exam: mild icterus, mild ascites, no asterixis.
Surveillance ultrasound today shows no focal lesion; AFP 5.8.
Plan: continue furosemide 40 bid, spironolactone 100, lactulose and rifaximin. Repeat ultrasound and AFP in 6 months. He remains abstinent.
Hepatology

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Welcome to Medicare Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
IPPE.
Interval: Ileostomy doing fine, output steady, reversal likely late summer. Graft on L leg mostly took; wound clinic weekly. Hepatology in May: no liver mass, AFP normal. Breathing unchanged.
Functional: independent with self-care, drives, does his own shopping. Uses no assistive device. No falls this year. Hearing ok, vision corrected.
Safety: smoke detectors, no firearms at home.
Advance directive: not done; gave him the health care proxy form to take home.
Screening: colon - under cancer surveillance. Prostate - under urology. Lung - he is still within 15 years of quitting, but given his cancer imaging and liver disease we agreed not to add separate screening CTs. AAA - n/a (never had one; not indicated by this exam, defer). Depression PHQ-2 1.
Vaccines: Tdap and Shingrix #1 today. Second Shingrix in 2-6 months. COVID series done.
Exam: BP and weight as charted. Lungs diminished, clear. Heart RRR. Abd soft, stoma healthy, mild ascites. L leg graft site pink, small open edge 0.5 cm. Feet: no lesions, sensation intact, pulses diminished.
Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UACR.
Plan: return after reversal.

Mr. Kimball returns four years after radical retropubic prostatectomy with adjuvant prostate-bed radiation. PSA 0.1 ng/mL, stable. No urinary complaints, no hematuria, no bone pain.
Impression: prostate adenocarcinoma in biochemical remission.
Plan: PSA yearly, return in 12 months.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Ileostomy Reversal
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Admit 08/24/2021, discharge 08/27/2021.
Procedure 08/24/2021: closure of diverting loop ileostomy. Pre-op contrast enema was not done because of iodinated contrast anaphylaxis; flexible sigmoidoscopy 08/03/2021 showed an intact, healed anastomosis.
Course: return of bowel function day 2, tolerating diet day 3. Lactulose resumed at home dose once stools began. No confusion this admission. Blood glucose 110-190 on basal plus correction.
Discharge: home medications unchanged. Stools are often frequent for a while after this operation; lactulose may need trimming - titrate to 3-4 soft BMs.
Follow-up: colorectal clinic 2 weeks, oncology surveillance per schedule, colonoscopy at one year from resection.
Colorectal Surgery
